sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Angular Sweep
sections.content: Introduce the idea of a line rotating around a point (pivot). Explain that the 'Windmill' is a line pivoted at one point in a set of points, rotating until it hits another point.
sections.example: A lighthouse beam (the line) rotating in the ocean, hitting different islands (the points) one by one.

sections.title: Defining the Windmill Mechanics
sections.content: Establish the rules: Given a set of points, pick one as a pivot. Rotate the line clockwise. When it hits a second point, that point becomes the new pivot, and the process repeats.
sections.example: Visualizing a clock hand that snaps to a new center point every time it strikes a target marker.

sections.title: Key Property: The Invariant of Order
sections.content: Explain the core observation: The sequence of points encountered depends on the initial angle. Highlight that the number of 'swaps' can be predicted using geometry.
sections.example: A chameleon on a rotating branch catching fireflies; the order of catches is determined by the starting orientation of the branch.

sections.title: Visualization of the Rotation
sections.content: Use a step-by-step animation sequence: (1) Select initial pivot, (2) Calculate angles to all other points, (3) Rotate line to smallest angle, (4) Update pivot. Focus on the geometry of the 'next hit'.
sections.example: A spider web where the string (the line) rotates and attaches to the next nearest anchor point on the web.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize the computational complexity (O(N^2) or O(N log N) depending on optimization). Discuss applications in robotics pathfinding and sensor coverage.
sections.example: A robot vacuum cleaner navigating a room filled with obstacles, using the windmill strategy to clear every corner.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Angular Sweep
lecture_lines: Imagine a line rotating around a pivot point.
The Windmill problem uses this rotation strategy.
A line strikes points in a set.
animations: Create a central pivot point labeled 'P' in #FFFFFF color.
Draw a set of lines through 'P' colored #FF4500.
Animate the lines rotating clockwise around 'P'.

storyboard.title: Defining the Windmill Mechanics
lecture_lines: We pick a point as the pivot.
The line rotates until it hits another point.
That second point becomes the new pivot.
animations: Rotate blades 30 degrees around central pivot 'P'.
Highlight pivot 'P' with a glowing effect in #FFFF00.

storyboard.title: Key Property: The Invariant of Order
lecture_lines: The rotation order depends on initial angle.
Geometry determines the sequence of points hit.
We can predict every pivot swap.
animations: Show clockwise and counter-clockwise orders of blades.
Demonstrate order invariance using colored arcs in #32CD32.
Confirm the invariant persists after a rotation.

storyboard.title: Visualization of the Rotation
lecture_lines: First, select an initial pivot point.
Calculate angles to all other points.
Rotate the line to the smallest angle.
Update the pivot to the hit point.
Repeat this process for the full set.
animations: Trace the path of each blade with a #FF00FF line.
Finalize the rotation cycle to show state preservation.

storyboard.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: The Windmill strategy is efficient to compute.
It helps robots navigate complex environments.
Sensors use this to cover every area.
animations: Summarize key points: Sweep, Pivot, Invariant.
Display a real-world windmill icon labeled 'W' in #FFA500.
End with the final state labeled 'Invariant' in #FFFFFF.
